old: It would be great if it were possible to go there with Tom, that I have known since the age of eight
new: It would be great if it were possible to go there with Tom, who I have known since the age of eight
reason: Non-defining relative after a comma needs who/whom, not 'that'

old: If a tourist came to London, I would recommend to him first to go for a walk along the Thames
new: If a tourist came to London, I would first recommend that he go for a walk along the Thames
reason: 'recommend to him to go' is not natural English

old: I intend to invite three friends from school, that I get on with really well, to London
new: I intend to invite three friends from school, who I get on with really well, to London
reason: Non-defining relative after a comma needs who, not 'that'

old: My cousins Charlie and Sophie, that I had not seen since the summer
new: My cousins Charlie and Sophie, whom I had not seen since the summer
reason: Non-defining relative after a comma needs whom, not 'that'

old: My grandmother, she is Scottish, so I also feel a bit Scottish
new: My grandmother, for her part, is Scottish, so I also feel a bit Scottish

old: je passerais toujours Noël en famille et le Nouvel An avec eux.
new: je passerais toujours Noël en famille et le Nouvel An avec mes amis.

old: I would always spend Christmas with my family and New Year with them.
new: I would always spend Christmas with my family and New Year with my friends.

old: For next New Year, I am planning to go to a party at Harry's house, a friend from the choir, who lives in London
